name: Applied Coastal and Ocean Sciences, Ph.D.

deadline.value: Fall 2027 application deadline is June 1, 2027, with an Application Priority Deadline of January 15, 2027 (applications opened September 1, 2026; complete applications are reviewed as received).

gre_general.value: 2026-2027 Graduate Catalogue explicitly states no standardized test scores (including GRE) are required for admission.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for coastal/ocean/environmental/earth sciences (ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Applicants should make initial contact with prospective faculty mentors across CMS-participating departments prior to applying.
supervisor.quote: Potential UNCW Faculty Mentor(s): Applicants should make initial contact with prospective faculty mentors prior to applying. Please contact the graduate program coordinator if you need assistance with this process.

also.quote: It is best to make initial contact with prospective faculty mentors prior to applying.

funding.value: No automatic program-wide stipend is published; Ph.D. students compete for faculty-funded Graduate Research Assistantships (which cover both NC Resident and Non-Resident tuition plus monthly stipend per Graduate School policy), departmental Teaching Assistantships, and Graduate School fellowships (e.g., Ahuja Academy of Water Quality Fellowship, New Scholar Award).
funding.quote: Graduate Research Assistants receive tuition support in addition to their monthly stipend. Students enrolled in master's programs will receive the equivalent of the NC Resident (In-State) portion of their tuition, while students enrolled in doctoral programs will receive both the NC Resident and NC Non-Resident portions of their tuition.

also.quote: A limited number of scholarships are available to students entering any of UNCW's graduate programs for the first time. Students do not apply for these scholarships. Instead, nominations originate with the departments, which submit their recommendations to the dean of the Graduate School.

entry_route.value: Open to STEM BA/BS (60-credit track) and MA/MS (40-credit track) graduates; bachelor's-only applicants upload a document stating 'No master's thesis', though the Program Details page notes successful applicants usually hold an M.S. in science or engineering.
entry_route.quote: Total credits required: | 60 post-baccalaureate degree | 40 post-master’s degree | Target audience: STEM graduates (BA/BS/MA/MS) with an interest in the application of ocean science to issues of societal relevance and potential application beyond academia.

also.quote: Successful program applicants have a master's degree in science or engineering with an interest in applying their knowledge of marine science to real-world issues.

notes: DHS STEM-designated Ph.D. (CIP 30.3201 Marine Sciences) hosted at UNCW's Center for Marine Science (CMS), spanning faculty across Biology & Marine Biology, Chemistry & Biochemistry, Earth & Ocean Sciences, Environmental Sciences, and Physics & Physical Oceanography.
